There is currently a great deal of interest in the theoretical and practical possibility of cloaking objects from the observation by electromagnetic waves. The basic idea of these invisibility devices \cite{glu1, glu2, le},\cite{pss1} is to use anisotropic {\it transformation media} whose permittivity and permeability $\var^{\lambda

This formalism allows us to settle in an unambiguous way the mathematical problems posed by the singularities of the inverse of the permittivity and the permeability of the {\it transformation media} on the boundary of the cloaked objects. We write Maxwell's equations in Schr"odinger form with the electromagnetic propagator playing the role of the Hamiltonian. We prove that the electromagnetic propagator outside of the cloaked objects is essentially self-adjoint. There is currently considerable interest in the theoretical and practical possibility of cloaking objects from observation by electromagnetic waves. The fundamental idea behind these invisibility devices \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1} is to use anisotropic {\it transformation media} whose permittivity and permeability, $\var^{\lambda
u}$ and $\mu^{\lambda
u}$, are obtained from those, $\var_0^{\lambda
u}$ and $\mu^{\lambda
u}_0$, of isotropic media through singular coordinate transformations.

In this paper, we study electromagnetic cloaking in the time domain using the formalism of time-dependent scattering theory. This formalism enables us to address, in an unambiguous manner, the mathematical problems arising from the singularities of the inverses of the permittivity and permeability of the {\it transformation media} on the boundaries of the cloaked objects. We formulate Maxwell’s equations in Schr"odinger form, with the electromagnetic propagator playing the role of the Hamiltonian. We prove that the electromagnetic propagator outside the cloaked objects is essentially self-adjoint. Moreover, its unique self-adjoint extension is unitarily equivalent to the electromagnetic propagator in the medium $\var_0^{\lambda
u}, \mu^{\lambda
u}_0$. Using this fact, and since the coordinate transformation is the identity outside a ball, we prove that the scattering operator is the identity.

Our results provide a rigorous proof that the construction of \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1} perfectly cloaks passive and active devices from observation by electromagnetic waves. Furthermore, we establish cloaking for general anisotropic materials. In particular, our results show that it is possible to cloak objects inside general crystals.

At present, substantial attention is being devoted to both the theoretical foundations and practical feasibility of making objects invisible to detection by electromagnetic waves. The central principle behind these cloaking devices \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1} is the employment of anisotropic {\it transformation media}. Their permittivity and permeability tensors, $\var^{\lambda\nu}$ and $\mu^{\lambda\nu}$, are produced from the corresponding tensors $\var_0^{\lambda\nu}$ and $\mu^{\lambda\nu}_0$ of isotropic media through singular changes of coordinates.

In this work, we investigate electromagnetic cloaking in the time domain within the framework of time-dependent scattering theory. This approach makes it possible to resolve, in a precise and non-ambiguous manner, the mathematical difficulties caused by the singular behavior of the inverses of the permittivity and permeability of the {\it transformation media} at the boundary of the hidden objects. Maxwell’s equations are formulated in Schr\"odinger form, where the electromagnetic propagator serves as the Hamiltonian.

We show that the electromagnetic propagator in the region exterior to the cloaked objects is essentially self-adjoint. In addition, its sole self-adjoint extension is unitarily equivalent to the electromagnetic propagator associated with the background medium $\var_0^{\lambda\nu}, \mu^{\lambda\nu}_0$. Combining this equivalence with the fact that the coordinate transformation reduces to the identity outside a ball, we establish that the scattering operator is the identity.

These results provide a rigorous demonstration that the cloaking scheme proposed in \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1} achieves perfect concealment of both passive and active devices from electromagnetic-wave observation. We also establish cloaking for arbitrary anisotropic materials. In particular, our analysis shows that objects can be cloaked even when placed inside general crystals.

There is significant scientific and technological interest in the possibility of using electromagnetic cloaking devices to conceal objects from detection by electromagnetic waves. Such devices are designed so that incident radiation is guided around a region of space, preventing waves from interacting with whatever is placed inside that region. As a result, an observer outside the cloak would ideally be unable to detect either the hidden object or the presence of the cloak itself.

The paper investigates this phenomenon from a rigorous mathematical perspective, focusing on electromagnetic cloaking in the time domain. This approach is important because many physical signals vary with time, and a complete theory of cloaking should apply not only to single-frequency waves but also to general time-dependent electromagnetic fields. The authors use time-dependent scattering theory to analyze the behavior of electromagnetic waves in cloaking media. A central difficulty addressed in the work is that ideal transformation-based cloaks require material parameters that become singular at the cloaking surface. These singularities create mathematical challenges in defining and solving Maxwell’s equations.

To handle these issues, Maxwell’s equations are reformulated in a Schrödinger-type form. In this formulation, the evolution of the electromagnetic field is described by an operator analogous to a Hamiltonian in quantum mechanics. This electromagnetic propagator governs the time evolution of the fields and provides a suitable framework for applying methods from spectral and scattering theory.

The authors prove that, outside the cloaked regions, the electromagnetic propagator is essentially self-adjoint. This means that the time evolution of the electromagnetic fields is uniquely determined by the physical system, despite the singular nature of the material parameters. They also show that the propagator for the cloaking medium is equivalent, in a precise mathematical sense, to the propagator associated with the original, uncloaked medium. This equivalence implies that electromagnetic waves outside the cloak behave exactly as if the cloaked region and its contents were not present.

The results provide a rigorous justification for transformation-media cloaking. In particular, they show that ideal cloaks can perfectly hide both passive objects and active devices placed inside the cloaked region. Moreover, the theory applies not only to simple isotropic backgrounds but also to more general anisotropic materials, including media such as crystals. Thus, the paper establishes a strong mathematical foundation for the claim that transformation-based electromagnetic cloaking can render a wide class of objects and devices completely invisible to external electromagnetic observations.

The paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework for electromagnetic cloaking in the time domain. Rather than studying only monochromatic waves or stationary solutions, it treats the full time-dependent evolution of electromagnetic fields. To do this, Maxwell’s equations are reformulated in a Schrödinger-type form, where the electromagnetic field evolves under a self-adjoint operator determined by the material parameters of the medium. This formulation is especially useful for cloaking problems because ideal cloaks are described by highly singular permittivity and permeability tensors at the cloaking interface.

A central difficulty addressed in the paper is the behavior of electromagnetic fields near the boundary of the cloaked region. In ideal transformation-based cloaking, the material parameters may become degenerate or unbounded at this boundary, so standard Maxwell theory in regular media is not directly applicable. The authors show how to define the electromagnetic dynamics in such singular media in a mathematically precise way. In particular, they prove that the exterior electromagnetic propagator is essentially self-adjoint. This means that the time evolution outside the cloaked region is uniquely determined by the initial electromagnetic field and does not require imposing extra boundary conditions at the cloaking surface.

The paper then establishes that the electromagnetic dynamics in the exterior of the cloak are unitarily equivalent to the dynamics in the original, uncloaked medium. This unitary equivalence shows that, from the point of view of an observer outside the cloak, waves propagate exactly as they would if the cloak and the cloaked object were absent. As a consequence, the scattering operator associated with the cloaking construction is the identity operator. In physical terms, incoming electromagnetic waves suffer no detectable scattering: they emerge as though they had propagated through empty space or through the original background medium.

This result provides a rigorous proof of perfect electromagnetic cloaking in the time domain. The analysis applies not only to passive objects hidden inside the cloaked region, but also to active devices, such as sources or electromagnetic systems that generate fields. The fields produced inside the cloaked region remain confined and cannot be detected from the exterior, while exterior waves are unaffected by the presence of the cloak.

The framework is broad enough to include general anisotropic media, including materials such as crystals whose electromagnetic response depends on direction. Thus, the paper extends the mathematical foundations of cloaking beyond simple isotropic models and demonstrates that ideal cloaking can be rigorously understood for a wide class of physically relevant materials. Overall, the work gives a precise time-dependent scattering-theoretic justification for perfect electromagnetic invisibility produced by singular transformation-optics media.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a mathematical physics paper proving electromagnetic cloaking via transformation media and time-dependent scattering theory, including self-adjointness of the Maxwell propagator and identity of the scattering operator.
counterfactuals.output:
We prove electromagnetic cloaking for Maxwell’s equations using transformation media and time-dependent scattering theory. Starting from a singular change of variables that blows up a point into a bounded cloaked region, we construct anisotropic, spatially inhomogeneous permittivity and permeability tensors whose degeneracies implement an ideal cloak. The corresponding Maxwell evolution is formulated as a unitary dynamics on the natural finite-energy Hilbert space. We establish essential self-adjointness, or equivalently uniqueness of the self-adjoint Maxwell propagator, for the exterior cloaking medium and characterize the induced boundary condition at the cloaking interface. This shows that finite-energy electromagnetic fields cannot exchange energy with the cloaked region.

We then compare the cloaking dynamics with the free Maxwell dynamics by means of wave operators. Using the unitary equivalence generated by the transformation map, we prove existence and completeness of the time-dependent wave operators and show that the associated scattering operator is the identity. Consequently, the ideal cloak produces no electromagnetic scattering at any frequency: incident finite-energy waves evolve outside the cloak exactly as if the cloaked object were absent, while the fields in the cloaked region remain dynamically decoupled from the exterior. These results give a rigorous operator-theoretic proof of perfect invisibility for transformation-optics media and clarify the role of self-adjointness, boundary conditions, and energy conservation in ideal electromagnetic cloaking.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.output:
\[
\textbf{Abstract.}
\]
We study rigorous invisibility cloaking for Maxwell's equations in anisotropic media generated by singular coordinate transformations. Starting from the transformation-optics formulation, we construct degenerate permittivity and permeability tensors obtained by blowing up a point or lower-dimensional set into a cloaked region. The resulting electromagnetic material parameters are anisotropic and singular at the cloaking interface, requiring a weak formulation of Maxwell's equations adapted to finite-energy fields. Within this framework, we prove that exterior electromagnetic measurements are invariant under the singular transformation and coincide with those in free space, thereby yielding ideal cloaking.

The analysis covers both passive objects, modeled by arbitrary regular material inclusions inside the cloaked region, and active devices, represented by internal sources or currents. We show that passive inclusions are completely hidden from boundary measurements, while active devices can also be cloaked provided the corresponding compatibility conditions for finite-energy Maxwell fields are satisfied. In particular, the singular anisotropic permittivity and permeability tensors decouple the cloaked region from the exterior domain in the appropriate weak sense. These results provide a mathematical foundation for transformation-optics cloaking of electromagnetic fields and clarify the role of degeneracy, anisotropy, and source compatibility in the rigorous treatment of ideal invisibility for Maxwell's equations.

This operator-theoretic perspective permits a direct treatment of causality, finite-energy solutions, and possible singular material coefficients without relying on time-harmonic assumptions. As a consequence, the cloaked dynamics outside the cloaking surface are indistinguishable from free-space propagation, while fields in the concealed region remain dynamically decoupled from exterior observations. **Abstract** — Transformation optics provides a rigorous mechanism for perfect electromagnetic cloaking by exploiting the form invariance of Maxwell’s equations under singular changes of variables. In the standard construction, a point or lower-dimensional set in a virtual electromagnetic space is “blown up” to a finite cloaked region in physical space. The push-forward of the background permittivity and permeability under this transformation produces material tensors that guide incident fields around the hidden domain and restore the exterior fields exactly to those of the uncloaked medium. Consequently, the cloak is perfectly invisible at the level of boundary measurements and scattering data.

A central mathematical feature of ideal cloaks is the singular behavior of the transformed constitutive parameters at the cloaking interface. Depending on the eigen-direction, the permittivity and permeability tensors may vanish or diverge, and their inverses may fail to be bounded. These boundary singularities are not technical artifacts but are essential to exact cloaking: they enforce the degeneracy needed to prevent electromagnetic energy from penetrating the cloaked region while maintaining compatibility with exterior Maxwell fields. In a weak or finite-energy formulation, the singular inverse tensors determine the admissible traces of the electric and magnetic fields at the inner boundary, yielding hidden boundary conditions that decouple the concealed region from the exterior. Thus, perfect cloaking is recovered not by ignoring the singularities, but by incorporating them into the functional framework of the transformed Maxwell system.

The same transformation-optical argument extends beyond isotropic backgrounds to general anisotropic media. If the original medium has arbitrary positive definite tensor-valued permittivity and permeability, such as those arising in crystalline materials, the transformed tensors are obtained by the same push-forward rule involving the Jacobian of the coordinate map. Maxwell’s equations retain their covariant structure, and the exterior electromagnetic response remains identical to that of the original anisotropic medium. Therefore, ideal cloaking is not restricted to scalar or isotropic materials: it is a geometric phenomenon valid for broad classes of anisotropic constitutive laws, provided the transformed tensors, including their controlled degeneracies at the cloak boundary, are interpreted in the appropriate weak sense.

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a rigorous mathematical physics abstract with citations placeholders like \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1}, describing essential self-adjointness of the electromagnetic propagator outside cloaked objects and showing the scattering operator is the identity.
counterfactuals.output:
We study the time-dependent Maxwell system on singular transformation-optics backgrounds modeling electromagnetic cloaks.  Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^{3}\) denote the exterior of a finite collection of cloaked regions, and let \(\varepsilon,\mu\) be the degenerate anisotropic material tensors obtained as push-forwards of the Euclidean tensors under the standard blow-up map.  The corresponding electromagnetic propagator is realized as the symmetric Maxwell operator
\[
A(E,H)= i\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\nabla\times H,\,-\mu^{-1}\nabla\times E\bigr)
\]
on the finite-energy Hilbert space
\[
\mathcal H_{\Omega}
  = L^{2}(\Omega,\varepsilon\,dx;\mathbb C^{3})
    \oplus L^{2}(\Omega,\mu\,dx;\mathbb C^{3}).
\]
We prove that the minimal operator \(A_{0}\), initially defined on smooth compactly supported fields away from the cloaking interface, is essentially self-adjoint.  Consequently, Maxwell evolution outside the cloaked bodies is uniquely determined by the exterior initial data, without imposing boundary conditions at the singular interface.  In particular, the cloaking surface is dynamically impenetrable: no finite-energy electromagnetic flux crosses it, and the interior degrees of freedom decouple from the exterior evolution.

The proof uses the unitary equivalence induced by the cloaking transformation between \(A_{0}\) and the free Maxwell generator on punctured Euclidean space.  Since sets of codimension at least three are removable for the finite-energy Maxwell dynamics, the transformed free operator is essentially self-adjoint; pulling back the unique self-adjoint closure yields essential self-adjointness of the physical cloaking Hamiltonian.  This argument provides a functional-analytic formulation of perfect invisibility consistent with the transformation-optics construction of ideal cloaks \cite{glu1, glu2, le} and with previous analyses of singular electromagnetic media \cite{pss1}.

As an application, we compare the full exterior dynamics with the free Maxwell dynamics in homogeneous space.  The wave operators
\[
W_{\pm}
  = \operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}
      e^{itA_{\mathrm{cloak}}}J e^{-itA_{\mathrm{free}}}
\]
exist and are complete for the natural identification \(J\) induced by the transformation map.  Moreover, the incoming and outgoing identifications coincide, and hence
\[
S = W_{+}^{*}W_{-}=I .
\]
Thus the ideal cloak has trivial scattering matrix: all scattering amplitudes vanish, the exterior fields evolve exactly as if the cloaked regions were absent, and the cloaked objects are electromagnetically undetectable by finite-energy measurements performed outside the cloak.
